status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The access failure/erroneous enforcement is unwanted behaviour engaging the repair benchmark. OpenAI reports mitigation and full recovery after the 105-minute login/account-creation incident. That is affirmative, source-bounded evidence of repair restoring service in this recovery stage; it does not establish cause, individual completeness beyond the report, or prevention of recurrence.

conclusion_change.previous: The evidenced boundary is service availability, not authority state. A login symptom does not establish that expired, suspended, restricted, unavailable or revoked states were conflated; that an authentication transition failed to propagate; or that an otherwise valid entitlement depended on a verifier that could not complete. The provider's distinct investigating, monitoring and resolved updates preserved a usable operational recovery state, while the undisclosed cause prevents a more specific mechanism adjudication. Both material clauses retain resolved-no-mapping dispositions. The occurrence is fully adjudicated but unclassified, which does not assert that every invariant held. Clear operational status updates and recovery do not establish all recognition conditions of an access-state success. No reviewed FC-derived candidate or independently source-identified admitted external requirement is established here; no external compliance finding is implied.
